<?php
require_once 'header.php';
require_once 'auth_check.php';
require_permission('manage_leads');

if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] !== 'POST') {
    redirect('leads.php');
}
verify_csrf();

$id = (int)($_POST['lead_id'] ?? 0);
$action = (string)($_POST['action'] ?? '');

$lead = fetch_one(
    "SELECT * FROM leads WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?",
    $id,
    $current_user->tenant_id
);
if (!$lead) {
    flash_set('danger', 'Lead not found.');
    redirect('leads.php');
}

$back = 'lead-view.php?id=' . $id;

function lead_action_redirect($back, $type, $message) {
    flash_set($type, $message);
    redirect($back);
}

try {
    switch ($action) {
        case 'add_activity':
            $allowed_types = ['call', 'whatsapp', 'email', 'sms', 'meeting', 'note'];
            $type = (string)($_POST['activity_type'] ?? 'note');
            if (!in_array($type, $allowed_types, true)) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Choose a valid follow-up type.');
            }
            $subject = trim((string)($_POST['subject'] ?? ''));
            $notes = trim((string)($_POST['notes'] ?? ''));
            $outcome = trim((string)($_POST['outcome'] ?? ''));
            $next = trim((string)($_POST['next_follow_up_at'] ?? ''));

            if ($subject === '' && $notes === '') {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Enter a subject or notes for the follow-up.');
            }
            if (mb_strlen($subject) > 191 || mb_strlen($outcome) > 100) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'The subject or outcome is too long.');
            }
            if ($next !== '' && !preg_match('/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/', $next)) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Next follow-up date is not valid.');
            }

            $is_contact = in_array($type, ['call', 'whatsapp', 'email', 'sms', 'meeting'], true);
            $conn->begin_transaction();
            try {
                record_lead_activity(
                    $id,
                    (int)$current_user->tenant_id,
                    $type,
                    $subject !== '' ? $subject : null,
                    $notes !== '' ? $notes : null,
                    $outcome !== '' ? $outcome : null,
                    null,
                    $next !== '' ? $next : null
                );
                if ($is_contact) {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET last_contacted_at = NOW(),
                                status = CASE WHEN status = 'new' THEN 'contacted' ELSE status END
                          WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('ii', $id, $current_user->tenant_id);
                    if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                    $stmt->close();
                }
                if ($next !== '') {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET next_follow_up_at = ? WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('sii', $next, $id, $current_user->tenant_id);
                    if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                    $stmt->close();
                }
                $conn->commit();
            } catch (Throwable $ex) {
                $conn->rollback();
                throw $ex;
            }
            audit_log('add_activity', 'lead', $id, 'Recorded ' . activity_type_label($type) . ' follow-up');
            lead_action_redirect($back, 'success', 'Follow-up recorded.');
            break;

        case 'assign':
            $assigned_to = (int)($_POST['assigned_to'] ?? 0);
            if ($assigned_to > 0 && !user_has_tenant_permission($assigned_to, 'manage_leads', (int)$current_user->tenant_id)) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'The selected staff member cannot be assigned leads.');
            }
            $current_assignee = (int)($lead['assigned_to'] ?? 0);
            if ($current_assignee === $assigned_to) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'info', 'The lead is already assigned to that staff member.');
            }
            $assignee_name = 'Unassigned';
            if ($assigned_to > 0) {
                $assignee = fetch_one(
                    "SELECT first_name, last_name, username FROM users WHERE user_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?",
                    $assigned_to,
                    $current_user->tenant_id
                );
                $assignee_name = trim(($assignee['first_name'] ?? '') . ' ' . ($assignee['last_name'] ?? '')) ?: ($assignee['username'] ?? ('User #' . $assigned_to));
            }

            $conn->begin_transaction();
            try {
                $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                    "UPDATE leads SET assigned_to = ? WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?"
                );
                $assigned_db = $assigned_to ?: null;
                $stmt->bind_param('iii', $assigned_db, $id, $current_user->tenant_id);
                if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                $stmt->close();
                record_lead_activity(
                    $id,
                    (int)$current_user->tenant_id,
                    'assignment',
                    'Assigned to ' . $assignee_name
                );
                $conn->commit();
            } catch (Throwable $ex) {
                $conn->rollback();
                throw $ex;
            }
            audit_log('assign', 'lead', $id, 'Assigned to ' . $assignee_name);
            lead_action_redirect($back, 'success', 'Lead assigned to ' . $assignee_name . '.');
            break;

        case 'set_status':
            $target = (string)($_POST['status'] ?? '');
            $statuses = lead_statuses();
            if (!isset($statuses[$target])) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Choose a valid lead status.');
            }
            $allowed = lead_allowed_transitions((string)$lead['status']);
            if (!in_array($target, $allowed, true)) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'That status change is not allowed from ' . $statuses[$lead['status']] . '.');
            }
            $lost_reason = trim((string)($_POST['lost_reason'] ?? ''));
            if ($target === 'lost' && mb_strlen($lost_reason) < 3) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Enter a reason of at least 3 characters when marking a lead lost.');
            }

            $conn->begin_transaction();
            try {
                if ($target === 'converted') {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET status = 'converted', converted_at = NOW(), lost_reason = NULL
                          WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND status = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('iis', $id, $current_user->tenant_id, $lead['status']);
                } elseif ($target === 'lost') {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET status = 'lost', lost_reason = ?
                          WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND status = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('siis', $lost_reason, $id, $current_user->tenant_id, $lead['status']);
                } elseif ($target === 'new') {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET status = 'new', lost_reason = NULL, converted_at = NULL
                          WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND status = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('iis', $id, $current_user->tenant_id, $lead['status']);
                } else {
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE leads SET status = ?
                          WHERE lead_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND status = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('siis', $target, $id, $current_user->tenant_id, $lead['status']);
                }
                if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                if ($stmt->affected_rows !== 1) throw new RuntimeException('This lead was changed by someone else. Reload and try again.');
                $stmt->close();

                record_lead_activity(
                    $id,
                    (int)$current_user->tenant_id,
                    'status_change',
                    'Status: ' . $statuses[$lead['status']] . ' → ' . $statuses[$target],
                    $target === 'lost' ? $lost_reason : null
                );
                $conn->commit();
            } catch (Throwable $ex) {
                $conn->rollback();
                throw $ex;
            }
            audit_log('set_status', 'lead', $id, 'Status changed to ' . $target);
            lead_action_redirect($back, 'success', 'Lead status updated to ' . $statuses[$target] . '.');
            break;

        case 'link_order':
        case 'unlink_order':
            if (!can('manage_orders')) {
                http_response_code(403);
                die('You do not have permission to manage order links.');
            }
            $order_id = (int)($_POST['order_id'] ?? 0);
            $order = fetch_one(
                "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_id = ? AND tenant_id = ?",
                $order_id,
                $current_user->tenant_id
            );
            if (!$order || !order_is_visible($order)) {
                lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'That order is not available to you.');
            }

            $conn->begin_transaction();
            try {
                if ($action === 'link_order') {
                    if (!empty($order['lead_id']) && (int)$order['lead_id'] !== $id) {
                        throw new RuntimeException('That order is already linked to another lead.');
                    }
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE orders SET lead_id = ?
                          WHERE order_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND (lead_id IS NULL OR lead_id = ?)"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('iiii', $id, $order_id, $current_user->tenant_id, $id);
                    if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                    $stmt->close();
                    record_lead_activity(
                        $id,
                        (int)$current_user->tenant_id,
                        'order_link',
                        'Order ' . $order['order_number'] . ' linked to lead',
                        null,
                        null,
                        $order_id
                    );
                    $message = 'Order ' . $order['order_number'] . ' linked.';
                } else {
                    if ((int)($order['lead_id'] ?? 0) !== $id) {
                        throw new RuntimeException('That order is not linked to this lead.');
                    }
                    $stmt = $conn->prepare(
                        "UPDATE orders SET lead_id = NULL
                          WHERE order_id = ? AND tenant_id = ? AND lead_id = ?"
                    );
                    $stmt->bind_param('iii', $order_id, $current_user->tenant_id, $id);
                    if (!$stmt->execute()) throw new RuntimeException($stmt->error);
                    $stmt->close();
                    record_lead_activity(
                        $id,
                        (int)$current_user->tenant_id,
                        'order_link',
                        'Order ' . $order['order_number'] . ' unlinked from lead',
                        null,
                        null,
                        $order_id
                    );
                    $message = 'Order ' . $order['order_number'] . ' unlinked.';
                }
                $conn->commit();
            } catch (Throwable $ex) {
                $conn->rollback();
                throw $ex;
            }
            audit_log($action, 'lead', $id, $message);
            lead_action_redirect($back, 'success', $message);
            break;

        default:
            lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', 'Unknown lead action.');
    }
} catch (Throwable $ex) {
    lead_action_redirect($back, 'danger', $ex->getMessage());
}

## Objective
- Implement and integrate staff-facing Orders and Leads modules into the existing DEZL BUSINESS SYSTEM PHP/MySQL application, without building the public storefront or unrelated features.
- Follow the user's full implementation brief: inspect first, reuse existing structures where suitable, implement working secure workflows, test locally, and report results.

## Requirements
- Scope is Orders and Leads only: no public catalogue, cart, guest checkout, public submission endpoint, or customer storefront; no transfers, returns, or new payment system.
- Orders must support unique human-readable reference, tenant association, optional contact link, customer name/phone/location snapshots, product lines/quantities, product/pricing snapshots, currency, optional shop/warehouse, source, status, timestamps, responsible staff, and safe sale/invoice link when possible.
- Use database-backed unique reference generation safe under concurrency; do not rely only on checking whether a string exists.
- Order lifecycle at minimum: New/requested, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Cancelled, Fulfilled; no arbitrary bypassing status changes.
- Orders must never deduct stock on creation/review; do not reserve stock in this task; do not mark fulfilled merely by status change; no duplicate invoices/sales on retry; do not fabricate unsafe POS/invoice integration.
- Leads must integrate with existing contact/CRM structures where appropriate: searchable/filterable list, open lead with contact/order, assign authorized staff, record contact attempts/follow-up notes, next follow-up date, status/outcome, link to order without duplicating order data, activity history.
- Lead and order remain conceptually distinct; either can exist without the other, and linking/unlinking must work.
- Add `manage_leads`; decide and explain whether separate `manage_orders` is necessary.
- Enforce permissions server-side, tenant-scope every query/mutation, respect shop scoping helpers, never trust submitted tenant/shop/warehouse IDs.
- Follow existing PHP/MySQL/MariaDB/Bootstrap/jQuery/navigation conventions; use prepared statements, CSRF, transactions, existing error handling; no public endpoints.
- Use existing migration conventions, additive/repeatable migration, safe rollback, no destructive changes, no production deployment or data modification.
- Test locally: CRUD, linking/unlinking, assignment/activities, valid/invalid transitions, duplicate references/submissions, invalid products/quantities/customers/shop-warehouse combos, tenant/shop isolation, unauthorized access, CSRF, transaction rollback, preservation of existing modules.
- Final report must cover existing structures, schema assessment, files, migrations/rollback, workflows, authorization, exact test results including untested items, known limitations, and next smallest step.
- Do not claim tests passed unless actually run and observed.

## Decisions
- No suitable existing Orders/Leads tables exist; `deals` is too thin and dormant, so `leads` is a new table rather than an extension of `deals`.
- Reuse dormant `activities` table as lead history by extending it with `lead_id`, `order_id`, `activity_type`, `notes`, `outcome`, indexes, and FKs.
- Create new `orders`, `order_items`, `leads`, and `document_sequences`; keep order and lead conceptually separate with `orders.lead_id` as the single link.
- Create both `manage_orders` and `manage_leads` permissions; rationale: order recording is a commercial operation distinct from CRM follow-up, and shop-scoped sales staff may need orders without full lead visibility.
- Order statuses: `new`, `under_review`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `fulfilled`.
- Allowed order transitions: `new`→`under_review`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `under_review`→`confirmed`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `confirmed`→`fulfilled`/`cancelled`; terminal states have none.
- Lead statuses: `new`, `contacted`, `qualified`, `converted`, `lost`, with validated transitions in `helpers.php`.
- Fulfilment only links an existing tenant/access-appropriate invoice; it never creates an invoice or moves stock. Unique `fulfilled_invoice_id` prevents duplicate linking.
- Order creation snapshots catalogue `sale_price`, tax rate, code, name, description, and unit; client-submitted prices are not trusted.
- Order numbering uses per-tenant `document_sequences` with `UPDATE ... SET next_value = LAST_INSERT_ID(next_value + 1)` inside a transaction, format `ORD-000001`; leads use `LEAD-000001`.
- One-time per-session form tokens plus PRG protect against duplicate staff submissions; CSRF protects every state-changing request.
- Order visibility: admins see all; non-admins see orders they created/assigned or in accessible shops. Leads are tenant-wide like existing contacts/customer visibility.
- Confirmation requires an accessible active shop and store, with store belonging to shop; no stock reservation.
- Reuse existing `contacts`, `users`, `shops`, `warehouses`, `inventory_stock`, `products`, `invoices`; do not modify their business data.
- Customer deletion guard should also consider linked orders/leads.
- Migration 003 initially failed with errno 121 due to FK name collisions with `pos_orders`; constraints were renamed `fk_cord_*` / `fk_coi_*`.
- `order_items` initially failed errno 150 because `orders` lacked unique `(order_id, tenant_id)`; that key was added before the composite child FK.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full read-only inspection of schema, config, helpers, auth, permissions, navigation, CRUD conventions, invoice/POS flows, and migration patterns.
- Confirmed no orders/leads tables; `deals`/`activities` dormant (0 rows locally); no `manage_orders`/`manage_leads` permissions.
- Created and applied `database/migrations/003_orders_leads.php` locally; it created `document_sequences`, `leads`, `orders`, `order_items`, extended `activities`, seeded sequences, added permissions/grants, and recorded `003_orders_leads` in `schema_migrations`.
- Created `database/migrations/003_orders_leads_rollback.php` with `--confirm=ROLLBACK_ORDERS_LEADS`, local-host guard, FK/index/column removal, table drops, permission/migration-record cleanup.
- Extended `helpers.php` with user-permission checks, sequence allocation, form tokens, order/lead statuses/transitions, visibility scoping, badges, source/activity labels, and `record_lead_activity()`.
- Created `orders.php` list with filters, scoped queries, badges, and actions.
- Created `order-add.php` with customer/contact snapshotting, shop/store validation, server-side product price snapshotting, duplicate-line merging, transaction, sequence allocation, form token, and lead-origin logging.
- Created `order-view.php` with snapshot/stock display, lead link/unlink, status actions, confirm shop/store form, invoice-link fulfilment form, and audit history.
- Created `order-edit.php` with editable customer/shop/store/notes/product lines only for `new`/`under_review`, transactionally replacing items.
- Local migration currently applied; no production changes made.
- No git repository exists; all work is uncommitted.

### Active
- Orders/Leads implementation in progress: remaining pages and integration/tests still to be written.
- `order-view.php` and `order-edit.php` have just been written; neither has yet been syntax-checked or tested.
- `order-add.php` bind_param type strings were manually corrected but not linted/tested.

### Blocked
- End-to-end local HTTP testing requires creating temporary test users with known passwords and starting a local PHP server; not yet done.
- No user decisions currently block implementation within the stated Orders/Leads scope.

## Next Move
1. Create `order-action.php` for CSRF-protected `start_review`, `confirm`, `reject`, `cancel`, `fulfil`, `link_lead`, and `unlink_lead`, with status-guarded updates and transaction/duplicate protection.
2. Create `leads.php`, `lead-add.php`, `lead-view.php`, `lead-edit.php`, and `lead-action.php` (activity logging, assignment, status transitions, order link/unlink).
3. Add Orders/Leads entries to `sidebar.php` and update `customers.php`/`customer-view.php` deletion guards and integration cards.
4. Run `php -l` on every changed/new PHP file.
5. Rerun migration 003 to verify idempotency, then test rollback and reapply.
6. Start local PHP server; create temporary admin and shop-scoped test users; run HTTP tests for CRUD, status transitions, duplicate tokens/references, invalid inputs, tenant/shop isolation, 403s, CSRF, rollback-on-duplicate-sequence, and preservation of existing modules.
7. Clean up test fixtures, confirm inventories/invoices/payments/POS unchanged, and deliver the required final report.

## Relevant Files
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\database\migrations\003_orders_leads.php`: applied migration for all new schema, permissions, sequences, and activities extension.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\database\migrations\003_orders_leads_rollback.php`: dev-only rollback, not yet tested.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\helpers.php`: new shared helpers for sequences, form tokens, scoping, statuses, and lead activity logging.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\orders.php`: implemented order list.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\order-add.php`: implemented order creation; needs lint/runtime test.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\order-view.php`: implemented order detail/actions UI; needs `order-action.php`.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\order-edit.php`: implemented order editing; syntax check needed.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\sidebar.php`: still needs Orders/Leads navigation entries.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\customers.php`: deletion guard still needs orders/leads checks.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\customer-view.php`: integration cards for linked orders/leads still to add.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\auth_check.php`: `require_permission`/`require_permission_any` guards used by new pages.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\invoice-add.php`: existing racy `invoice_next_number` pattern intentionally not reused.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\database\schema_business_v2.sql`: baseline schema reference; not updated by migrations.
- `C:\xampp\htdocs\business\pos-session.php`: fixed shop/store POS workflow and access-check reference.

## Important Context
- Local DB `u839560293_agensupply` on MariaDB `10.4.32`; PHP CLI `C:\xampp\php\php.exe` (`8.2.12`); DB user `root`, blank password.
- Migration 003 is applied locally; order/lead tables exist and permissions were granted to the single existing role.
- InnoDB FK constraint names are database-wide: existing `pos_orders` uses `fk_orders_tenant`/`fk_orders_contact`, so new order constraints use `fk_cord_*` and order-item constraints use `fk_coi_*`.
- `orders` has unique `(order_id, tenant_id)`, required by `order_items` composite FK.
- `activities` is referenced by `users.php` user-deletion guard; lead activities will therefore block deleting users with history, consistent with existing behavior.
- `config.php` has production `BASE_URL` but local DB credentials; redirects are relative, so local built-in server testing is viable.
- Root webroot exposes sensitive seed scripts/SQL dump/audit Markdown; do not add sensitive docs to webroot.
- Test fixtures must not modify existing product/contact/inventory data; use direct SQL inserts for invoice-link tests to avoid stock deductions, then clean up fixtures.
- `order-add.php`/`order-edit.php` use `store_label()`, `accessible_shops()`, `accessible_stores()`, `find_accessible_store()`, `shop_is_accessible()`, `accessible_warehouse_ids()`, `tenant_admin_scope()`, `csrf_field()`, `verify_csrf()`.
- `order-view.php` currently links to `lead-view.php`, which does not exist yet.
- `order-action.php` is referenced by `order-view.php` but has not been created yet.

## Objective
- Implement and integrate staff-facing Orders and Leads modules into the existing DEZL BUSINESS SYSTEM PHP/MySQL application, without building the public storefront or unrelated features.
- Follow the user's full implementation brief: inspect first, reuse existing structures where suitable, implement working secure workflows, test locally, and report exact results.

## Requirements
- Scope is Orders and Leads only: no public catalogue, cart, guest checkout, public submission endpoint, or customer storefront; no transfers, returns, or new payment system.
- Orders need unique human-readable reference, tenant association, optional contact link, customer name/phone/location snapshots, product lines/quantities, product/pricing snapshots, currency, optional shop/warehouse, source, status, timestamps, responsible staff, and safe sale/invoice link where possible.
- Reference generation must be database-backed and concurrency-safe; do not rely only on checking whether a string exists.
- Order lifecycle at minimum: New/requested, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Cancelled, Fulfilled; no arbitrary bypassing status changes.
- Orders must never deduct stock on creation/review; do not reserve stock; do not mark fulfilled merely by status change; no duplicate invoices/sales on retry; do not fabricate unsafe POS/invoice integration.
- Leads must integrate with existing contact/CRM structures: searchable/filterable list, open lead with contact/order, assign authorized staff, record contact attempts/follow-up notes, next follow-up date, status/outcome, link to order without duplicating order data, activity history.
- Lead and order remain conceptually distinct; either can exist without the other, and linking/unlinking must work.
- Add `manage_leads`; decide and explain whether separate `manage_orders` is necessary.
- Enforce permissions server-side, tenant-scope every query/mutation, respect shop-scoping helpers, never trust submitted tenant/shop/warehouse IDs.
- Follow existing PHP/MySQL/MariaDB/Bootstrap/jQuery/navigation conventions; use prepared statements, CSRF, transactions, existing error handling; no public endpoints.
- Use existing migration conventions, additive/repeatable migration, safe rollback, no destructive changes, no production deployment or data modification.
- Test locally: CRUD, linking/unlinking, assignment/activities, valid/invalid transitions, duplicate references/submissions, invalid products/quantities/customers/shop-warehouse combos, tenant/shop isolation, unauthorized access, CSRF, transaction rollback, preservation of existing modules.
- Final report must cover existing structures, schema assessment, files, migrations/rollback, workflows, authorization, exact test results including untested items, known limitations, and next smallest step.
- Do not claim tests passed unless actually run and observed.

## Decisions
- No suitable existing Orders/Leads tables exist; `deals` is too thin and dormant, so `leads` is a new table rather than an extension of `deals`.
- Reuse dormant `activities` table as lead history by extending it with `lead_id`, `order_id`, `activity_type`, `notes`, `outcome`, indexes, and FKs.
- Create new `orders`, `order_items`, `leads`, and `document_sequences`; keep order and lead separate with `orders.lead_id` as the single link.
- Create both `manage_orders` and `manage_leads` permissions; order recording is a commercial operation distinct from CRM follow-up, and shop-scoped sales staff may need orders without full lead visibility.
- Order statuses: `new`, `under_review`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `fulfilled`.
- Allowed order transitions: `new`→`under_review`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `under_review`→`confirmed`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `confirmed`→`fulfilled`/`cancelled`; terminal states have none.
- Lead statuses: `new`, `contacted`, `qualified`, `converted`, `lost`, with validated transitions in `helpers.php`; lost leads can reopen to new.
- Fulfilment only links an existing tenant/access-appropriate invoice; it never creates an invoice or moves stock. Unique `fulfilled_invoice_id` prevents duplicate linking.
- Order creation snapshots catalogue `sale_price`, tax rate, code, name, description, and unit; client-submitted prices are not trusted.
- Order numbering uses per-tenant `document_sequences` with `UPDATE ... SET next_value = LAST_INSERT_ID(next_value + 1)` inside a transaction, format `ORD-000001`; leads use `LEAD-000001`.
- One-time per-session form tokens plus PRG protect against duplicate staff submissions; CSRF protects every state-changing request.
- Order visibility: admins see all; non-admins see orders they created/assigned or in accessible shops. Leads are tenant-wide like existing contacts/customer visibility.
- Confirmation requires an accessible active shop and store, with store belonging to shop; no stock reservation.
- Lead-related order UI is gated by `manage_orders`: lead-only users cannot view/link order details. Linking from order-view requires `manage_leads`; linking from lead-action requires `manage_orders`.
- Order editing is limited to `new`/`under_review`, with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` to prevent concurrent status bypass.
- Reuse existing `contacts`, `users`, `shops`, `warehouses`, `inventory_stock`, `products`, `invoices`; do not modify their business data.
- Customer deletion guard now also blocks contacts linked to orders/leads.
- Migration 003 initially failed with errno 121 due to FK name collisions with `pos_orders`; constraints were renamed `fk_cord_*` / `fk_coi_*`.
- `order_items` initially failed errno 150 because `orders` lacked unique `(order_id, tenant_id)`; that key was added before the composite child FK.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full read-only inspection of schema, config, helpers, auth, permissions, navigation, CRUD conventions, invoice/POS flows, and migration patterns.
- Confirmed no orders/leads tables; `deals`/`activities` dormant; no prior `manage_orders`/`manage_leads` permissions.
- Created and applied `database/migrations/003_orders_leads.php` locally; it created `document_sequences`, `leads`, `orders`, `order_items`, extended `activities`, seeded sequences, added permissions/grants, and recorded `003_orders_leads` in `schema_migrations`.
- Created `database/migrations/003_orders_leads_rollback.php` with `--confirm=ROLLBACK_ORDERS_LEADS`, local-host guard, FK/index/column removal, table drops, permission/migration-record cleanup.
- Extended `helpers.php` with permission checks, sequence allocation, form tokens, order/lead statuses/transitions, visibility scoping, badges, source/activity labels, and `record_lead_activity()`.
- Implemented `orders.php`, `order-add.php`, `order-view.php`, `order-edit.php`, and `order-action.php`.
- Implemented `leads.php`, `lead-add.php`, `lead-view.php`, `lead-edit.php`, and `lead-action.php`.
- Added Orders/Leads sidebar entries and active-page handling.
- Updated `customers.php` deletion guard and added Orders/Leads cards to `customer-view.php`, gated by permissions.
- Ran `php -l` successfully on all changed/new PHP files and both migrations.
- Created local test fixtures: role `zz_shop_role` (manage_orders, manage_leads, manage_contacts, manage_pos, view_dashboard), role `zz_noperm_role` (view_dashboard only), users `zz_admin` (id 9, admin role), `zz_shop` (id 10, member of shop 1), `zz_noperm` (id 11); password `TestPass!234`; shop1=1, shop2=7.
- Started local PHP built-in server at `http://127.0.0.1:8081/` (background shell ID `sh_17cfd487900178lS4v75kqCTHn`).
- Authored a broad HTTP/DB integration harness covering creation, validation, duplicate tokens, lifecycle, editing, leads, scoping, CSRF, cross-tenant access, duplicate references, and existing-module smoke tests.

### Active

- Integration tests have not yet been confirmed as complete or passing.

# Orders & Leads — Implementation Report

## 1. Existing structure assessment

The existing system already had the pieces needed to integrate without inventing a parallel CRM or sales stack:

- `contacts` for customers/CRM records
- `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_shops`
- `shops`, `warehouses` and existing shop/warehouse scoping helpers
- `products`, `inventory_stock`, `inventory_movements`
- `invoices`, `payments`, `pos_orders`
- A dormant `activities` table
- A dormant `deals` table

There were **no usable orders or leads tables**. `deals` was too thin and dormant to serve as a lead pipeline, and extending it would not have provided order lines, lifecycle, sequencing or tenant-safe references. I therefore:

- Created `orders`, `order_items`, `leads` and `document_sequences`.
- Reused and extended `activities` for lead/order history rather than creating a duplicate history table.
- Left `deals` untouched.

No public catalogue, cart, checkout, guest submission endpoint or customer storefront was added.

---

## 2. Files created

New application files:

- `orders.php` — searchable/filterable order list
- `order-add.php` — order creation
- `order-view.php` — order detail, lifecycle actions, invoice linking, lead linking
- `order-edit.php` — editing only `new` / `under_review` orders
- `order-action.php` — CSRF-protected status changes and linking actions
- `leads.php` — searchable/filterable lead list
- `lead-add.php` — lead creation, contact prefill
- `lead-view.php` — lead detail, assignment, follow-ups, linked orders, history
- `lead-edit.php` — contact/source/follow-up editing
- `lead-action.php` — activity, status, assignment, order link/unlink actions
- `database/migrations/003_orders_leads.php`
- `database/migrations/003_orders_leads_rollback.php`

Files modified:

- `helpers.php` — permissions, sequence allocation, form tokens, statuses/transitions, visibility scoping, badges, activity logging
- `sidebar.php` — Orders and Leads navigation
- `customers.php` — deletion guard now blocks contacts linked to orders/leads
- `customer-view.php` — permission-gated Orders and Leads cards

No changes were made to invoice creation, POS logic, payments or inventory movement logic.

---

## 3. Schema and migrations

### New tables

**`orders`**

Key fields:

- `order_id`, `tenant_id`, `order_number`
- `contact_id`, `lead_id`
- `customer_name`, `customer_phone`, `customer_location`, `customer_email`
- `source`, `status`, `currency_code`
- `subtotal`, `total`
- `shop_id`, `warehouse_id`
- `notes`, `assigned_to`, `created_by`
- confirmation/rejection/cancellation/fulfilment audit fields
- `fulfilled_invoice_id`
- timestamps

Important constraints and indexes:

- `UNIQUE uq_order_number (tenant_id, order_number)`
- `UNIQUE uq_order_tenant (order_id, tenant_id)`
- `UNIQUE uq_order_invoice (fulfilled_invoice_id)` — prevents one invoice being linked to two orders
- indexes for status, shop, assignment, creation date

**`order_items`**

- `tenant_id`, `order_id`, `line_no`, `product_id`
- product code/name/description/unit snapshots
- `quantity`, `unit_price`, `tax_rate_snapshot`, `line_total`, `notes`
- `UNIQUE uq_order_line (order_id, tenant_id, line_no)`

**`leads`**

- `lead_number`, `tenant_id`, `contact_id`
- contact name/company/phone/email/location snapshots
- `source`, `status`, `assigned_to`
- `next_follow_up_at`, `last_contacted_at`, `notes`
- `lost_reason`, `converted_at`, `created_by`
- timestamps
- `UNIQUE uq_lead_number (tenant_id, lead_number)`

**`document_sequences`**

- Primary key `(tenant_id, sequence_key)`
- `next_value`

Order references use `ORD-000001`; leads use `LEAD-000001`.

Generation is database-backed inside the order/lead transaction:

```sql
UPDATE document_sequences
SET next_value = LAST_INSERT_ID(next_value + 1)
WHERE tenant_id = ? AND sequence_key = ?

SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID()
```

This avoids relying on “check whether the string exists”.

**`activities` extension**

- `lead_id`
- `order_id`
- `activity_type`
- `notes`
- `outcome`
- indexes and foreign keys

The rollback has a local-host guard and requires the explicit confirmation flag. It is destructive for order/lead history by design.

---

## 4. Workflows

### Orders

Lifecycle:

```text
new -> under_review | rejected | cancelled
under_review -> confirmed | rejected | cancelled
confirmed -> fulfilled | cancelled
rejected / cancelled / fulfilled -> terminal
```

Editable only in `new` and `under_review`. Editing uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` so a concurrent status change cannot be bypassed.

Creation:

- snapshots customer details
- snapshots product code, name, description, unit, catalogue price and tax rate
- ignores client-submitted prices
- validates products, quantities, customer, shop and warehouse
- does not reserve or deduct stock
- creates no invoice, sale, payment or stock movement
- uses one-time form tokens plus PRG to prevent duplicate submissions

Confirmation:

- requires an accessible active shop and store
- verifies the store belongs to the selected shop
- still performs no stock reservation or deduction

Fulfilment:

- requires an existing accessible invoice
- links that invoice only
- never creates an invoice and never moves stock
- rejects already-linked invoices through both application checks and the unique constraint

### Leads

Lifecycle:

```text
new -> contacted | qualified | lost
contacted -> qualified | converted | lost
qualified -> converted | lost
converted -> terminal
lost -> new (reopen)
```

Leads support:

- contact search/prefill
- assignment to a tenant user holding `manage_leads`
- contact attempts and follow-up notes
- next follow-up date and last-contacted date
- outcome and status changes
- activity history
- linked orders without duplicating order data
- unlink, relink and conversion to a linked order

Leads and orders remain separate records. `orders.lead_id` is the single link; leads do not store duplicate order data.

---

## 5. Authorization and security

### Permissions

Added:

- `manage_orders`
- `manage_leads`

I intentionally kept them separate:

- Order recording is a commercial/shop-scoped operation.
- Lead follow-up is CRM work.
- A shop sales user may need to record orders without seeing or managing the full lead pipeline.
- A CRM user may manage leads without being allowed to create or confirm orders.

Migration grants:

- `manage_orders` to existing roles holding `manage_pos`, `manage_invoices`, `manage_settings` or `manage_users`
- `manage_leads` to existing roles holding `manage_contacts`, `manage_settings` or `manage_users`

### Access control

- Every order/lead page requires authentication plus the relevant permission.
- All queries include `tenant_id`.
- Submitted tenant IDs are never trusted.
- Shop and store IDs are validated against accessible shop/store helpers.
- Admins see all orders.
- Non-admin order visibility: creator, assignee, or an accessible shop.
- Leads are tenant-wide, consistent with contacts/CRM visibility.
- Lead order panels are hidden without `manage_orders`.
- Order-to-lead linking requires `manage_leads`.
- Lead-to-order linking requires `manage_orders`.
- All state-changing POSTs verify CSRF.
- Customer deletion now refuses contacts linked to orders or leads.

Prepared statements are used throughout, with integer casting where dynamic `IN` lists are built.

---

## 6. Observed test results

Environment:

- Windows
- PHP `8.2.12`
- MariaDB `10.4.32`
- Local database `u839560293_agensupply`
- Local PHP server `http://127.0.0.1:8081/`
- Synthetic test users, roles, shop and cross-tenant records; all removed afterwards

### Integration suite

Final run after a fresh migration reapply:

```text
=== RESULT: 97 passed, 0 failed ===
```

Coverage included:

- login and permission denial
- Order list/creation pages
- valid order creation and redirect
- `ORD-######` numbering
- initial `new` status
- customer snapshot
- server-side catalogue pricing
- product snapshot
- order/item counts
- no stock or movement changes
- replayed form token rejection
- invalid product, zero quantity, cross-shop store
- missing/invalid CSRF
- non-existent customer
- lifecycle transitions
- confirm without store rejected
- double confirmation rejected
- fulfil without invoice rejected
- valid fulfilment links invoice
- re-fulfilment rejected
- reject/cancel paths
- edit form, snapshot re-capture, item replacement, unchanged order number
- lead creation, invalid customer, invalid email
- duplicate lead form token rejection
- assignment, activities, notes, follow-up dates
- lead status transitions
- lead/order link and unlink from both directions
- duplicate order-link rejection
- lead and order filters
- shop-scoped access restrictions
- unauthorized user 403s
- cross-tenant order/lead visibility and actions
- duplicate order number DB rejection
- duplicate invoice linking rejection
- customer deletion guard with lead history
- existing pages: customers, customer view, products, sales, invoices, inventory
- stock and movement fingerprint unchanged

No PHP warnings, notices or fatal errors appeared in the final test log or server log.

### Concurrent order submission

```text
CONCURRENCY RESULT: 5 passed, 0 failed
```

Two simultaneous HTTP order submissions both saved and received unique numbers `ORD-000007` and `ORD-000008`.

### Concurrent sequence allocation

Four separate PHP processes each allocated 10 order numbers simultaneously:

```text
SEQUENCE CONCURRENCY RESULT: 4 passed, 0 failed
range: ORD-000009 .. ORD-000048
```

All 40 numbers were unique and correctly formatted.

### Transaction rollback

A temporary database trigger forced an `order_items` insert failure during order creation:

```text
TRANSACTION RESULT: 7 passed, 0 failed
```

Observed:

- forced failure surfaced as a form error
- no order row remained
- no order item row remained
- sequence increment was rolled back
- removing the trigger allowed a retry
- retry created exactly one order
- stock fingerprint unchanged

### Migration and rollback

Observed:

- migration 003 applied successfully from scratch
- rerunning it completes without duplicating tables/columns/permissions
- permissions remain present and grants are additive
- rollback removes `orders`, `order_items`, `leads`, `document_sequences`, activity extension columns/FKs, permissions and migration record
- rollback deletes linked lead/order activity rows
- existing `contacts`, `products`, `invoices`, `payments`, `pos_orders`, `inventory_stock`, `inventory_movements`, `shops`, `warehouses`, `users` tables remain
- stock fingerprint before and after rollback was identical:

```text
7f389fe6b30fd19df0ed25791469910b
```

- migration was re-applied successfully after rollback testing

### Syntax checks

All changed/new PHP files and both migrations passed:

```text
No syntax errors detected
```

Sixteen files checked in total.

### Final smoke test

After cleanup:

- login succeeded
- `orders.php` — 200
- `leads.php` — 200
- `order-add.php` — 200
- `lead-add.php` — 200
- `customers.php`, `sales.php`, `inventory.php` — 200
- sidebar showed Orders and Leads

---

## 7. Final local state

- Migration `003_orders_leads` is applied and recorded in `schema_migrations`.
- Permissions `manage_orders` and `manage_leads` exist.
- `Administrator` role holds both.
- Test users, test roles, test tenants, test invoices, test orders/leads and test activities were removed.
- Final counts: 1 tenant, 1 user, 1 contact, 1 product, 1 stock row, 1 movement, 0 orders, 0 order items, 0 leads, 0 activities.
- Local PHP test server was stopped.
- No production or staging deployment was performed.
- No production data was modified.
- The workspace is not a git repository, so no commit was created.

---

## 8. Known limitations and untested items

- UI testing was HTTP-level, not real-browser DOM/jQuery interaction testing.
- No lead-number HTTP concurrency test was run; lead numbering uses the same database sequence mechanism tested for orders.
- No long-running load/soak test was performed. Concurrency testing covered 2 simultaneous HTTP posts and 40 concurrent sequence allocations.
- The temporary test harnesses live outside the webroot and were not added to a committed automated test suite.
- Order `total` currently equals `subtotal`. Line tax rates are snapshotted, but tax is not added to the order total. If the business requires tax-inclusive order totals, that is a deliberate follow-up change.
- Fulfilment only links an existing invoice. It cannot create an invoice or move stock.
- No email/SMS notifications, file attachments or automated lead follow-up scheduling were added.
- Orders have no soft-delete/archive workflow.
- Shop-scoped users cannot see an unassigned order with no shop unless they created it; this is intentional.
- The pre-existing customer delete action is a GET route without CSRF. I only added the new order/lead deletion guard; changing the existing route was outside scope.
- Rollback is destructive for all order/lead history by design and is restricted to local/dev hosts.

---

## 9. Next smallest step

Before any production deployment, run migration 003 on a **staging copy with a verified backup**, then have one administrator create a real order, confirm it with a shop/store, link an existing invoice, create a lead, assign it, log a follow-up, and link/unlink an order.

After that, the smallest code follow-up would be adding a small checked-in smoke/regression script for the order and lead happy paths plus authorization checks.

### Additional Requirement: Storefront Default Page and Login Placement

**1. Default landing page**

When a visitor opens the storefront's main URL, the application must display the public product catalogue immediately.

- The root storefront URL should open the product listing, not the staff login page or dashboard.
- Customers must be able to browse and search products without logging in.
- The catalogue must load directly without requiring the customer to navigate through another page first.
- Preserve the existing staff login route and authentication behavior.

**2. Login button in the top-right corner**

Add a clearly visible **Login** link or button at the top-right of the storefront header.

The header should contain:
- Business logo and name on the left, if available.
- Product search and cart access in an appropriate position.
- A **Login** button at the top-right on desktop.
- A responsive layout on mobile that keeps Login accessible without cluttering the header.

**3. Login behavior**

- Clicking Login opens the existing staff login page.
- Do not create a separate authentication system or duplicate login page.
- After staff login, users should enter the existing staff application according to its current authentication and authorization rules.
- Public customers must not be required to log in to browse products, use the cart, or submit an order request.
- Keep the storefront cart and checkout flow separate from staff-only pages and permissions.

**4. Routing and regression checks**

- Test opening the root storefront URL in a fresh browser session.
- Verify that the product catalogue appears without authentication.
- Verify that Login is visible in the top-right corner on desktop and accessible on mobile.
- Verify that Login opens the existing staff login route.
- Verify that existing staff login, logout, and protected administration pages continue to work.
- Verify that customers can complete guest checkout without signing in.

// ============================================================
// Shared helper functions
// ============================================================

/** Escape output for safe HTML rendering. */
function e($value) {
    return htmlspecialchars((string)$value, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');
}

/** Format a number as money using the tenant currency. */
function money($amount, $currency = 'TZS') {
    return $currency . ' ' . number_format((float)$amount, 2);
}

/** Get current tenant's currency code (cached per request). */
function tenant_currency() {
    global $conn, $current_user;
    static $currency = null;
    if ($currency !== null) return $currency;
    $currency = 'TZS';
    if (isset($current_user->tenant_id)) {
        $stmt = $conn->prepare("SELECT currency_code FROM tenants WHERE tenant_id = ?");
        $stmt->bind_param('i', $current_user->tenant_id);
        $stmt->execute();
        $row = $stmt->get_result()->fetch_assoc();
        if ($row) $currency = $row['currency_code'];
        $stmt->close();
    }
    return $currency;
}

/** Whether the business charges tax (VAT) on sales and invoices (cached per request). */
function tax_enabled() {
    global $conn, $current_user;
    static $enabled = null;
    if ($enabled !== null) return $enabled;
    $enabled = true;
    if (isset($current_user->tenant_id)) {
        $row = fetch_one("SELECT apply_tax FROM system_settings WHERE tenant_id = ?", $current_user->tenant_id);
        if ($row !== null) $enabled = (int)$row['apply_tax'] === 1;
    }
    return $enabled;
}

/** Set a one-time flash message. */
function flash_set($type, $message) {
    $_SESSION['flash'] = ['type' => $type, 'message' => $message];
}

/** Get and clear the flash message. */
function flash_get() {
    if (!empty($_SESSION['flash'])) {
        $f = $_SESSION['flash'];
        unset($_SESSION['flash']);
        return $f;
    }
    return null;
}

/** Redirect and stop execution. */
function redirect($url) {
    while (ob_get_level() > 0) {
        ob_end_clean();
    }
    header('Location: ' . $url);
    exit;
}

/** Check a permission on behalf of the current user. */
function can($permission) {
    global $current_user;
    return $current_user && $current_user->hasPermission($permission);
}

/** True when the user has tenant-wide shop visibility (full administrators). */
function tenant_admin_scope() {
    return can('manage_users') || can('manage_settings');
}

/**
 * Shops the current user may access.
 * Full administrators see every shop; other users see only mapped shops.
 */
function accessible_shops($tenant_id = null, $include_inactive = false) {
    global $current_user;
    if (!$current_user) return [];
    $tenant_id = $tenant_id === null ? (int)$current_user->tenant_id : (int)$tenant_id;
    if ($tenant_id !== (int)$current_user->tenant_id) return [];
    $active_sql = $include_inactive ? '' : ' AND s.is_active = 1';
    if (tenant_admin_scope()) {
        return fetch_all(
            "SELECT s.* FROM shops s WHERE s.tenant_id = ?{$active_sql} ORDER BY s.name",
            $tenant_id
        );
    }
    return fetch_all(
        "SELECT s.* FROM shops s
         JOIN user_shops us ON us.shop_id = s.shop_id AND us.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
         WHERE s.tenant_id = ? AND us.user_id = ?{$active_sql}
         ORDER BY s.name",
        $tenant_id,
        $current_user->user_id
    );
}

/** IDs of shops the current user may access. */
function accessible_shop_ids($tenant_id = null, $include_inactive = false) {
    return array_map(
        fn($row) => (int)$row['shop_id'],
        accessible_shops($tenant_id, $include_inactive)
    );
}

/**
 * Stores (warehouses) the current user may access.
 * Pass $shop_id to restrict to one shop.
 */
function accessible_stores($shop_id = null, $include_inactive = false, $tenant_id = null) {
    global $current_user;
    if (!$current_user) return [];
    $tenant_id = $tenant_id === null ? (int)$current_user->tenant_id : (int)$tenant_id;
    if ($tenant_id !== (int)$current_user->tenant_id) return [];

    $shops = accessible_shops($tenant_id, $include_inactive);
    if (!$shops) return [];
    $shop_ids = array_map(fn($row) => (int)$row['shop_id'], $shops);
    $placeholders = implode(',', array_fill(0, count($shop_ids), '?'));

    $sql = "SELECT w.*, s.name shop_name, s.code shop_code, s.is_active shop_is_active
            FROM warehouses w
            JOIN shops s ON s.shop_id = w.shop_id AND s.tenant_id = w.tenant_id
            WHERE w.tenant_id = ? AND w.shop_id IN ({$placeholders})";
    $params = array_merge([$tenant_id], $shop_ids);
    if (!$include_inactive) {
        $sql .= " AND w.is_active = 1 AND s.is_active = 1";
    }
    if ($shop_id !== null) {
        $sql .= " AND w.shop_id = ?";
        $params[] = (int)$shop_id;
    }

/**
 * Warehouse IDs for scoping list/report queries.
 * Returns null for a full administrator (no restriction), or an array

function accessible_warehouse_ids($tenant_id = null, $include_inactive = true) {
    if (tenant_admin_scope()) return null;

/** Whether the current user may access a shop. */
function shop_is_accessible($shop_id, $include_inactive = true) {
    global $current_user;

## Objective
- Implement and integrate staff-facing Orders and Leads modules into the existing DEZL BUSINESS SYSTEM PHP/MySQL application, without building the public storefront or unrelated features.
- Complete local verification, clean up test data, and report exact results, limitations, and the next step.

## Requirements
- Scope is Orders and Leads only: no public catalogue, cart, guest checkout, public submission endpoint, customer storefront, transfers, returns, or new payment system.
- Orders need unique human-readable reference, tenant association, optional contact link, customer name/phone/location snapshots, product lines/quantities, product/pricing snapshots, currency, optional shop/warehouse, source, status, timestamps, responsible staff, and safe sale/invoice link where possible.
- Reference generation must be database-backed and concurrency-safe; do not rely only on checking whether a string exists.
- Order lifecycle at minimum: New/requested, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Cancelled, Fulfilled; no arbitrary bypassing status changes.
- Orders must never deduct stock, reserve stock, or mark fulfilled merely by status change; no duplicate invoices/sales on retry; do not fabricate unsafe POS/invoice integration.
- Leads must integrate with contacts/CRM: searchable/filterable list, contact/order link, authorized assignment, contact attempts/follow-up notes, next follow-up date, status/outcome, linked order without duplicating order data, activity history.
- Lead and order remain conceptually distinct; either can exist without the other; linking/unlinking must work.
- Add `manage_leads`; decide and explain whether separate `manage_orders` is necessary.
- Enforce permissions server-side, tenant-scope every query/mutation, respect shop-scoping helpers, never trust submitted tenant/shop/warehouse IDs.
- Follow existing PHP/MySQL/MariaDB/Bootstrap/jQuery/navigation conventions; use prepared statements, CSRF, transactions, existing error handling; no public endpoints.
- Use existing migration conventions, additive/repeatable migration, safe rollback, no destructive changes, no production deployment or production data modification.
- Test locally: CRUD, linking/unlinking, assignment/activities, valid/invalid transitions, duplicate references/submissions, invalid products/quantities/customers/shop-warehouse combos, tenant/shop isolation, unauthorized access, CSRF, transaction rollback, preservation of existing modules.
- Final report must cover existing structures, schema assessment, files, migrations/rollback, workflows, authorization, exact test results including untested items, known limitations, and next smallest step.
- Do not claim tests passed unless actually run and observed.

## Decisions
- `deals` was too thin/dormant; create new `leads` rather than extending it.
- Reuse dormant `activities` as lead/order history by adding `lead_id`, `order_id`, `activity_type`, `notes`, `outcome`, indexes and FKs.
- Create `orders`, `order_items`, `leads`, `document_sequences`; keep order and lead separate with `orders.lead_id` as the single link.
- Create both `manage_orders` and `manage_leads`; order recording is a commercial/shop-scoped operation distinct from CRM follow-up.
- Order statuses: `new`, `under_review`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `fulfilled`.
- Allowed order transitions: `new`→`under_review`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `under_review`→`confirmed`/`rejected`/`cancelled`; `confirmed`→`fulfilled`/`cancelled`; terminal states have none.
- Lead statuses: `new`, `contacted`, `qualified`, `converted`, `lost`; lost leads can reopen to new.
- Fulfilment only links an existing tenant/access-appropriate invoice; never creates an invoice or moves stock.
- Order creation snapshots catalogue `sale_price`, tax rate, code, name, description, and unit; client-submitted prices are not trusted.

<?php
// ============================================================
// Public storefront helpers
//
// These helpers are deliberately separate from the staff POS/cart. The
// storefront only creates order requests; it never touches stock, sales,
// invoices or staff permissions.
// ============================================================

/**
 * The tenant whose catalogue is exposed at the public root URL.
 *
 * The application is single-business per installation. Use the first tenant
 * that has settings configured, with the lowest tenant_id as a deterministic
 * fallback. All public queries still filter by this tenant_id explicitly.
 */
function storefront_tenant() {
    static $loaded = false;
    static $tenant = null;
    if ($loaded) return $tenant;
    $loaded = true;

    $tenant = fetch_one(
        "SELECT t.*
           FROM tenants t
           LEFT JOIN system_settings s ON s.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
          ORDER BY (s.setting_id IS NULL) ASC, t.tenant_id ASC
          LIMIT 1"
    );
    return $tenant;
}

/** Storefront settings with safe defaults when no settings row exists. */
function storefront_settings($tenant) {
    $tenant_id = (int)($tenant['tenant_id'] ?? 0);
    $settings = $tenant_id > 0
        ? fetch_one("SELECT * FROM system_settings WHERE tenant_id = ? LIMIT 1", $tenant_id)
        : null;

    if (!$settings) {
        $settings = [
            'company_name'     => (string)($tenant['name'] ?? APP_NAME),
            'company_email'    => (string)($tenant['email'] ?? ''),
            'company_phone'    => (string)($tenant['phone'] ?? ''),
            'company_address'  => (string)($tenant['address'] ?? ''),
            'default_currency' => (string)($tenant['currency_code'] ?? 'TZS'),
            'logo_path'        => null,
        ];
    }
    return $settings;
}

/** Currency used by the public catalogue. */
function storefront_currency($tenant, $settings = null) {
    if (is_array($settings) && !empty($settings['default_currency'])) {
        return (string)$settings['default_currency'];
    }
    return (string)($tenant['currency_code'] ?? 'TZS');
}

/** Cart contents as product_id => quantity, with defensive cleanup. */
function storefront_cart() {
    $raw = $_SESSION['storefront_cart'] ?? [];
    if (!is_array($raw)) return [];

    $cart = [];
    foreach ($raw as $product_id => $quantity) {
        $product_id = (int)$product_id;
        $quantity = (int)$quantity;
        if ($product_id > 0 && $quantity > 0) {
            $cart[$product_id] = min(999, $quantity);
        }
    }
    return $cart;
}

/** Total number of units in the public cart. */
function storefront_cart_count() {
    return array_sum(storefront_cart());
}

/** Path to a valid, locally stored image; empty when unavailable. */
function storefront_image_path($path) {
    $path = trim((string)$path);
    if ($path === '') return '';
    $path = str_replace('\\', '/', $path);
    if (strpos($path, '..') !== false) return '';
    if (preg_match('#^https?://#i', $path)) return $path;
    return file_exists(__DIR__ . '/' . ltrim($path, '/')) ? ltrim($path, '/') : '';
}

/** The configured logo, or the built-in logo fallback. */
function storefront_logo($settings) {
    $logo = storefront_image_path($settings['logo_path'] ?? '');
    if ($logo !== '') return $logo;
    return file_exists(__DIR__ . '/assets/images/logo.png') ? 'assets/images/logo.png' : '';
}

/** Common SELECT for public product rows. */
function storefront_product_select() {
    return "SELECT p.*, c.name AS category_name, u.name AS unit_name, u.short_name AS unit_short,
                   COALESCE((
                       SELECT SUM(s.quantity)
                         FROM inventory_stock s
                        WHERE s.product_id = p.product_id
                          AND s.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
                   ), 0) AS stock_qty
              FROM products p
              LEFT JOIN product_categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id AND c.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
              LEFT JOIN units_of_measurement u ON u.unit_id = p.unit_id AND u.tenant_id = p.tenant_id";
}

/** Active products for the public catalogue, optionally searched/filtered. */
function storefront_products($tenant_id, $query = '', $category_id = 0) {
    $sql = storefront_product_select() . " WHERE p.tenant_id = ? AND p.is_active = 1";
    $params = [(int)$tenant_id];

    $query = trim((string)$query);
    if ($query !== '') {
        $like = '%' . mb_substr($query, 0, 100) . '%';
        $sql .= " AND (p.name LIKE ? OR p.code LIKE ? OR p.sku LIKE ? OR p.barcode LIKE ? OR p.description LIKE ?)";
        array_push($params, $like, $like, $like, $like, $like);
    }
    if ((int)$category_id > 0) {
        $sql .= " AND p.category_id = ?";
        $params[] = (int)$category_id;
    }
    $sql .= " ORDER BY p.name ASC, p.product_id ASC LIMIT 200";
    return fetch_all($sql, ...$params);
}

/** One active public product, or null when it is not in this tenant's catalogue. */
function storefront_product($tenant_id, $product_id) {
    return fetch_one(
        storefront_product_select() . " WHERE p.tenant_id = ? AND p.product_id = ? AND p.is_active = 1 LIMIT 1",
        (int)$tenant_id,
        (int)$product_id
    );
}

/** Public product categories for the tenant. */
function storefront_categories($tenant_id) {
    return fetch_all(
        "SELECT category_id, name
           FROM product_categories
          WHERE tenant_id = ?
          ORDER BY name ASC",
        (int)$tenant_id
    );
}

/** Whether an active product can be added to an order request. */
function storefront_available($product) {
    if (!$product) return false;
    if ((int)$product['is_service'] === 1) return true;
    return (float)($product['stock_qty'] ?? 0) > 0;
}

/**
 * Current cart rows with fresh catalogue prices.
 * Returns [items, missing_product_ids].
 */
function storefront_cart_details($tenant_id) {
    $items = [];
    $missing = [];
    foreach (storefront_cart() as $product_id => $quantity) {
        $product = storefront_product($tenant_id, $product_id);
        if (!$product) {
            $missing[] = (int)$product_id;
            continue;
        }
        $product['cart_quantity'] = (int)$quantity;
        $product['line_total'] = round((float)$product['sale_price'] * (int)$quantity, 2);
        $items[] = $product;
    }
    return [$items, $missing];
}

/** Sum of the current cart lines. */
function storefront_cart_subtotal($items) {
    $subtotal = 0.0;
    foreach ($items as $item) {
        $subtotal += (float)$item['line_total'];
    }
    return round($subtotal, 2);
}

    } elseif (!storefront_available($sf_product)) {

    } else {
        $sf_cart[$sf_product_id] = min(999, (int)($sf_cart[$sf_product_id] ?? 0) + $sf_quantity);
        flash_set('success', $sf_product['name'] . ' was added to your cart.');
